digest.component_or_area: Event store and enrichment queue reduction
propositions: Queue and digest events accumulate per ticket without deletion, but accumulation is small (median 2–3 events, max 32) and physical deletion reclaims no repository space since blobs remain in git history

Read cost is asymmetric: digest_sidecar scans newest-first and opens 1 file; queue reduction via _events_of opens all matching files per ticket (4,977 opens measured) and is called per reduce operation, breaching the 20 ms drain-gate budget (404–692 ms observed)

The queue reduction is latest-wins per event type and filenames carry monotonic timestamps identical to event bodies, so a newest-first suffix-lazy reader needs only 1 file per type per ticket with claim arbitration bounded by the contention window, eliminating unbounded read growth without deleting or renaming any committed events

Deletion-based retention schemes (physical prune, retire renames for sidecar events) are rejected: they violate invariant I1 or reclaim no storage; only compaction's deterministic source-derived rename pattern is merge-safe, but it is dominated by the read-bound design
The read-bound design is pure read behavior change with no writes, renames, or deletes, so it cannot regress the two-clone reconvergence regression; reconvergence is preserved unchanged
The 20 ms drain-gate budget breach persists because listdir dominates over opens at today's scale; that lever (store index or cheaper gate) is deferred as a separate follow-up
